_comment: One table of folder layouts, read by BOTH suites, so the Settings page can
never tell you a layout is broken that the server would have accepted.
`incoming/` holds the owner's only copy of every raw sub and is strictly
read-only (AGENTS.md §10). The library tree and the state folder are the
opposite — the app prunes caches, thumbnails and stack outputs inside the
library and rewrites config.json in the state folder — so nesting one inside
the other would make a correctly-scoped clean-up resolve inside the raw
folder. `nested_incoming_conflict` (webapp/config.py) refuses that save and
stays the authority; `folderConflict` (frontend/src/settingsFolders.ts) asks
the same question while you type, so the answer arrives beside the field
instead of as a red toast afterwards.
The two are NOT required to agree in both directions, and the table says
which way each case runs. A browser cannot resolve a symlink, a bind mount
or a case-insensitive filesystem, so the client is allowed to stay silent
where the server refuses ('server' cases below). It is never allowed to
claim a conflict the server would accept — that would block a good layout on
a guess, which is why every 'both' and 'neither' case is pinned on both
sides.
Readers: tests/webapp/test_config_upgrade.py and
frontend/src/settingsFolders.test.ts.
Each case is {incoming, library, data_root, verdict, field}. Blank strings
mean the field is left empty, which resolves to <data root>/incoming and
<data root>/library on both sides. `verdict` is 'both' (client and server
flag it), 'neither' (both accept), or 'server' (only the server can tell).
`field` names which form field the client marks, for the 'both' cases.

cases._why: a sibling whose name merely starts the same — a string prefix test would wrongly block this
one-directional: incoming inside the library is the app's own default shape one level up
a blank library resolves under the data root, which is itself inside incoming
a relative path resolves against the server's cwd, which a browser cannot know
`..` needs the real filesystem to resolve safely — the client declines rather than guesses
